prerequisites: Good command of school mathematics; ability to handle real numbers, simple functions such as polynomials, geometric concepts such as planes, lines, and circles; ability to perform algebraic transformations and calculate with powers.

learning_outcomes.text: Practice in the application-oriented use of what has been learned to concrete problems.
Apply mathematical methods to address questions in selected areas of mechanical engineering.
Perform algebraic transformations and sketch calculation steps.
Represent basic concepts of real and complex numbers.
Represent the concept of function and fundamental function types.
Determine derivatives of functions of one variable.
Calculate integrals of functions of one variable.
Plan and execute mathematical solutions for given application examples.
Determine advanced mathematical tools of engineering sciences based on case studies in individual, partner, and group work.
Explain and present their own calculation method for calculation examples in their own words.
Name and discuss necessary steps for calculations.
Implement improvements to calculations under guidance and through peer feedback.

syllabus_topics: Differential calculus of functions of one variable
Integral calculus of functions of one variable
teaching_methods: Lecture on the theoretical foundations and basic tools of the aforementioned contents, as well as illustration of their application using (engineering) examples.
Practicing what has been learned by independently solving practice problems.
Performance control through regular homework, board performance, tests possible.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with calculation examples and theory questions
